name: Secure Signal Admin API
description: Next.js Route Handlers backing the Secure Signal admin/authority dashboard. All authenticated routes rely on Supabase SSR cookies — include the session cookie set by /login on every request.

authentication.notes: Sign in via the web app or POST to /auth (Supabase hosted). The browser automatically attaches the sb-access-token cookie. Server-only routes verify it via createServerClient() and read role from public.profiles.

commonErrors.400: Validation failed — body did not match the Zod schema.
commonErrors.403: Forbidden — signed in but role not allowed for this resource.
commonErrors.500: Server or upstream (Supabase/Stripe/FCM) error. Body shape: { error: string }.

endpoints.description: OAuth callback URL used by Supabase after email-link / OAuth sign in. Exchanges the `code` query param for a session cookie and redirects to `next` or `/`.

query.code: string (required) — Supabase auth code from the redirect URL
query.next: string (optional) — path to redirect to after exchange, default `/`

responses.302: Redirect to origin + next (or /login?error=oauth on failure)

endpoints.description: List the signed-in user's emergency contacts.
Add an emergency contact for the signed-in user.
Update one of the signed-in user's emergency contacts.
Device-side incident ingestion. Writes an incident row with a PostGIS POINT location. Optionally links to a device via device_uuid.
endpoints.auth: public (device key recommended in v2 — currently RLS allows public insert)

body.device_uuid: string (optional) — looks up devices.device_uuid, attaches device_id

201.data: Incident (id, location, user_id, device_id, status='received', read=false, occurred_at)

endpoints.description: List incidents. Optional date filter (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Returns up to 500 rows newest first.
endpoints.auth: staff (admin/authority) or owner — enforced by RLS

query.date: string (optional) — YYYY-MM-DD UTC; filters occurred_at to that day

endpoints.description: Transition an incident between `received` and `reported`. Marks the row read. Writes a `logs` entry.
Send a ping to a device. Inserts a `pings` row (status=sent) and best-effort FCM push using the most recent token in `notifications`.
Device callback — marks a ping as `received`. Called by the device after processing the FCM push.
Public contact form submission. Stores a row in `contacts` for the admin Settings tab.
Stripe webhook endpoint. Verifies signature with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, upserts `subscriptions` rows, writes a logs entry.

subscriptionMetadata.supabase_user_id: Required key in subscription.metadata so the webhook can attach the row to a profile.

Incident.location: geography(Point, 4326) — PostGIS; EWKT string in API responses, parse with regex /POINT\(([-\d.]+)\s+([-\d.]+)\)/

admin: subscription: read all, write via Stripe webhook

notes: RLS is the source of truth for row-level access. Route handlers also enforce role checks server-side.
Geolocation fields are PostGIS — when you see 'SRID=4326;POINT(lng lat)' in insert bodies, that is EWKT. Read responses stringify the same.
Stripe webhook requires the raw request body — Next.js route handlers receive it via req.text().
FCM uses firebase-admin (server-only). The web client config you provided earlier is NOT compatible with admin — paste the service account JSON to populate FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY.
Use `application/json` content-type on all write requests.
